question: The Chinese traveler who visited Harsha's court was: (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Hiuen Tsang
Hao
Fa-Hien
I-Tsing
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Hiuen Tsang

Explanation:
Hiuen Tsang, a Chinese Buddhist monk and traveler, visited India in the 7th century. He visited the court of King Harshavardhana (ruled 606-647 CE). Hiuen Tsang provided detailed accounts of India's social, religious, and political life during his travels, documented in his book "Si-Yu-Ki" (Records of the Western World). He is also famous for studying at the Nalanda University. He attended the religious assemblies organized by Harsha at Kannauj and Prayag. Fa-Hien visited India during the Gupta period, while I-Tsing came later.

☛ Book by Hiuen Tsang → Si-Yu-Ki (Records of the Western World)
☛ Ruler during Hiuen Tsang's visit → Harshavardhana
☛ Chinese traveler who studied at Nalanda → Hiuen Tsang
☛ First Chinese traveler to India → Fa-Hien
question_hi: हर्ष के दरबार में आने वाला चीनी यात्री कौन था? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: ह्वेन त्सांग
हाओ
फ़ा-हियान
इत्सिंग
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है ह्वेन त्सांग

Explanation:
ह्वेन त्सांग एक चीनी बौद्ध भिक्षु और यात्री थे, जो 7वीं शताब्दी में भारत आए। उन्होंने राजा हर्षवर्धन (जिन्होंने 606-647 ई. तक शासन किया) के दरबार का दौरा किया। ह्वेन त्सांग ने अपनी यात्रा के दौरान भारत के सामाजिक, धार्मिक और राजनीतिक जीवन का विस्तृत विवरण लिखा, जो उनकी पुस्तक "सी-यू-की" (पश्चिमी दुनिया का रिकॉर्ड) में संग्रहित है। वे नालंदा विश्वविद्यालय में अध्ययन करने के लिए भी प्रसिद्ध हैं। ह्वेन त्सांग ने कन्नौज और प्रयाग में हर्ष द्वारा आयोजित धार्मिक सभाओं में भाग लिया। फा-हियान गुप्त काल में भारत आए, जबकि इत्सिंग बाद में आए।

question: Which of the following caves contain rock cut paintings dating back to the stone age era? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Barabar caves
Bhimbetka caves
Ajanta caves
Ellora caves
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bhimbetka caves

Explanation:
The Bhimbetka caves, located in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, are renowned for their Stone Age rock paintings, estimated to be around 30,000 years old. These paintings depict human life, hunting, dancing, and animal scenes. The site was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003. Barabar caves belong to the Mauryan period, while Ajanta and Ellora caves are associated with Buddhism, Jainism, and Hinduism, dating to later periods.

question: Which dynasty replaced the Shungas in Magadha? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Kushanas
Guptas
Kanvas
Satavahanas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kanvas

Explanation:
After the Shunga dynasty, the Kanva dynasty ruled over Magadha. The last Shunga ruler Devabhuti was killed by his minister Vasudeva Kanva, who founded the Kanva dynasty. The Kanvas ruled from 72 BCE to 28 BCE for about 45 years. There were four Kanva rulers: Vasudeva, Bhumimitra, Narayana, and Susarman. The last ruler Susarman was defeated by the Satavahana ruler Simuka, after which the Satavahanas rose to power in Magadha. Thus, the Kanva dynasty was a short-lived ruling dynasty in Magadha with limited historical significance.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who founded the Kanva dynasty? → Vasudeva Kanva
☛ What was the period of Kanva rule? → 72 BCE to 28 BCE
☛ Who was the last Kanva ruler? → Susarman
☛ Who ended the Kanva dynasty? → Satavahana ruler Simuka
☛ How many rulers did the Kanva dynasty have? → Four
question_hi: मगध में शुंगों के बाद किस वंश ने शासन किया? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: कुषाण
गुप्त
कण्व
सातवाहन
solution_hi:

Explanation:
मगध में शुंग वंश के बाद कण्व वंश ने शासन किया। शुंग वंश के अंतिम शासक देवभूति की हत्या उसके मंत्री वसुदेव कण्व ने की, जिसने कण्व वंश की स्थापना की। कण्व वंश ने 72 ईसा पूर्व से 28 ईसा पूर्व तक लगभग 45 वर्षों तक शासन किया। इस वंश के चार शासक हुए: वसुदेव, भूमिमित्र, नारायण और सुशर्मा। अंतिम शासक सुशर्मा को सातवाहन शासक सिमुक ने हराया, जिसके बाद मगध में सातवाहन वंश का उदय हुआ। इस प्रकार कण्व वंश मगध का एक लघु कालीन शासक वंश था, जिसका इतिहास में सीमित महत्व है।

question: Which ancient civilisations flourished in the Thar Desert area about 5000 years ago? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Babylonian Civilisation
Indus Valley Civilisation
Greek Civilisation
Egyptian Civilisation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indus Valley Civilisation

Explanation:
About 5000 years ago, the Indus Valley Civilisation flourished in the Thar Desert region. This civilisation was spread across present-day Pakistan and northwest India, with major cities like Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Kalibangan, and Lothal located near the Thar Desert. It is known for its advanced urban planning, drainage systems, trade, and script. Other options like Babylonian, Greek, and Egyptian civilisations were geographically distant from the Thar region.

question: Ashok Pillar of Delhi has baffled scientists as it weathers all vagaries of weather and yet does not rust or corrode. Which is it made of? (RRB NTPC Tier I (22/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: Iron
Bronze
Terracotta
Single rock stone
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Iron

Explanation:
The Ashok Pillar of Delhi is made of iron, which has baffled scientists because it has not rusted or corroded despite being exposed to the elements for about 1600 years. This pillar was built during the Gupta period (around 402 AD) and stands 7.21 meters tall, weighing approximately 6 tonnes. The secret of its preservation lies in its high phosphorus content and the formation of a thin protective layer of iron oxide that prevents further oxidation and moisture from reaching the metal. It is located in the Qutub Minar complex in Delhi.

☛ Ashok Pillar (Delhi) material → Iron
☛ Age of the pillar → About 1600 years
☛ Reason for preservation → High phosphorus content and protective oxide layer
☛ Location → Qutub Minar complex, Delhi
☛ Construction period → Gupta period (402 AD)

question: Which states were ruled by the earlier Chera dynasty?A. Tamil Nadu and KeralaB. Bengal and OrissaC. Arunachal Pradesh and SikkimD. Maharashtra and Gujarat (RRB NTPC Tier I (18/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: B
C
A
D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

Explanation:
The ancient Chera dynasty ruled over the regions of present-day Tamil Nadu and Kerala in South India. It was one of the three major Sangam period kingdoms, with its capital at Vanji. The Cheras were known for their maritime trade, especially with the Romans and Greeks. Prominent rulers included Nedum Cheral Adan and Senguttuvan, who is credited with introducing the worship of Pattini Devi. The Cheras exported spices, pearls, and ivory. The dynasty declined around the 3rd century CE and was later overshadowed by the Pandyas and Cholas.

question: Jataka tales are related to _____  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (29/12/2020) Shift 2)
options: Buddhism
Sikhism
Hinduism
Jainism
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Buddhism

Explanation:
Jataka tales are related to Buddhism. These stories describe the previous births of Gautama Buddha, where he is born as various beings and imparts moral lessons. Each Jataka tale depicts the actions and consequences of Buddha's past lives, helping to understand Buddhism's principles of karma and rebirth. Jataka tales are an important part of Buddhist literature and are used to explain the ethical and philosophical aspects of Buddhism in simple language.

question: Who was the founder of the Vishishtadvaita philosophy? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (30/12/2020) Shift 1)
options: Vishnu Swami
Madhvacharya
Ramanujacharya
Nimbarka
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ramanujacharya

Explanation:
The founder of the Vishishtadvaita philosophy was Ramanujacharya (1017-1137 CE). This school is one of the three main branches of Vedanta. Ramanujacharya refuted Adi Shankaracharya's Advaita Vedanta, asserting that Brahman is saguna (with attributes) and savishesha (with distinctions). According to him, the individual soul (jiva) and the world (jagat) are real and form the body of Brahman. He founded the Sri Vaishnava tradition and emphasized bhakti (devotion) and prapatti (surrender). His major works include the Shri Bhashya, Gitabhashya, and Vedarthasamgraha. Vishishtadvaita recognizes three realities: chit (sentient), achit (insentient), and Brahman. Ramanujacharya incorporated the Pancharatra Agama and the tradition of the Tamil Alvar saints.

question: During whose reign did the Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang visit India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Harshavardhana
Pulakesin II
Vikramaditya
Kirtivarman
solution:

Explanation:
The Chinese Buddhist monk and traveller Hiuen Tsang (also known as Xuanzang) visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana (606–647 CE), a prominent ruler of North India. Hiuen Tsang travelled to India between 630 and 645 CE and spent considerable time at Harsha's court. He described Harsha's administration, religious tolerance, and patronage of Buddhism in detail. Hiuen Tsang also visited and studied at the famous Nalanda University. His work 'Si-yu-ki' (Great Tang Records on the Western Regions) is a valuable source for Indian history and culture. Harshavardhana ruled from Thaneswar and Kannauj, and belonged to the Pushyabhuti dynasty.
